status_summary: After the 90-day pause ordered on 2025-01-20, NPR reported that more than 80 percent of USAID programs had been terminated by 2025-07-01, when USAID's remaining operations were merged into the State Department. Congress enacted the Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28) on 2025-07-24, rescinding about 7.9 billion dollars of foreign assistance funds, including 2.5 billion dollars for Development Assistance, 1.65 billion dollars for the Economic Support Fund and 496 million dollars for International Disaster Assistance. After a special message of 2025-08-28 proposing to rescind further foreign aid funds and a district court order of 2025-09-03 requiring obligation of expiring aid funds, the Supreme Court on 2025-09-26 stayed that order as to the funds in the special message (a preliminary ruling, not on the merits; no D.C. Circuit merits ruling was found). The FY2026 appropriations law (Public Law 119-75, H.R. 7148, enacted 2026-02-03) provided about 50 billion dollars for diplomacy and foreign assistance, which WOLA, an advocacy group, calculates is about 9.3 billion dollars below the prior year and almost 60 percent above the administration's 31.5 billion dollar request, and it merged International Disaster Assistance and Migration and Refugee Assistance into a new International Humanitarian Assistance account of about 5.4 billion dollars. Inference: Congress funded the 150 Account well above what the administration sought, so the enacted cut is smaller than the proposed cut, and whether total spending reached the Mandate's 2019 benchmark has not been established. For FY2027, a CRS report describes a request of about 37.8 billion dollars for national security, State and related programs, down about 27 percent from FY2026 enacted levels, and says the House passed H.R. 8595 on 2026-07-15 with about 49.2 billion dollars in new budget authority; it reports no Senate action. Inference: the program terminations and the end of USAID as a separate agency go further than the budget reduction the Mandate described.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14169 paused new obligations and disbursements of foreign development assistance for a 90-day review (published 2025-01-30).
NPR reported that more than 80% of USAID's programs had been terminated as the agency closed.

Public Law 119-28 (Rescissions Act of 2025) rescinded about $7.9 billion in foreign assistance and related funds, including Development Assistance $2.5 billion, Economic Support Fund $1.65 billion, Migration and Refugee Assistance $800 million, Global Health Programs $500 million, International Disaster Assistance $496 million and USAID operating expenses $125 million.
The President sent Congress a special message proposing to rescind additional foreign assistance funds; a district court issued an order on 2025-09-03 concerning the funds covered by that message.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-75, the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 7148), is approved; WOLA identifies H.R. 7148 as the bill carrying FY2026 State and foreign operations funding. The govinfo page does not list the act's divisions, and funding levels were not checked against the statute.

The FY2026 State and foreign operations act was signed; an advocacy-group analysis (WOLA, published 2026-02-19) says it provides about 50 billion dollars for diplomacy and assistance, nearly 9.3 billion dollars below prior-year levels excluding rescissions and almost 60 percent above the administration's 31.5 billion dollar request, and merges International Disaster Assistance and Migration and Refugee Assistance into a new International Humanitarian Assistance account of about 5.4 billion dollars.

The House passes H.R. 8595, FY2027 national security, State and related programs appropriations, with about 49.2 billion dollars in new budget authority, against an administration request of about 37.8 billion dollars (CRS); no Senate action reported as of the CRS report dated 2026-07-30.

title: Cut USAID and foreign aid spending toward 2019 levels and trim the 150 Account
uncertainties: The dollar size of the 2025-08-28 special message (commonly reported as several billion dollars) was not in the sources I could open, so I did not state it. FY2026 enacted foreign assistance totals, FY2027 request totals, and the 2019 comparison were not retrieved (State and Congress.gov pages were blocked, and a GAO page was rate limited). I did not verify GAO's view of the pocket rescission or the D.C. Circuit's ruling on the merits. The Rescissions Act total of about $7.9 billion is the sum of foreign-assistance paragraphs 1 to 19 as I read them from the statute; the Corporation for Public Broadcasting rescission is not included. The FY2026 level of about $50 billion and the merged account figure come from a WOLA analysis, not the statute; the FY2019 benchmark amount was not retrieved.
